newsitem.title: USA: Musicland in talks with lenders.
newsitem.headline: Musicland in talks with lenders.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp, which operates 1,392 stores, said Thursday it is seeking additional financing but the outcome of talks with its lenders is uncertain.

"We are currently negotiating with our banks regarding additional financing and modification or waivers of loan covenants, which are critical to the execution of our plans this fall," said Jack Eugster, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.
"At this time, the outcome of our bank group negotiations is uncertain," he said.

Musicland reported a net loss for the first quarter of $21 million, or $0.63 a share, compared with a loss of $52.6 million, or $1.58 a share, a year earlier. Last year's first quarter included a $35 million pretax restructuring charge related to the company's store closing program.
The narrower first quarter loss reflects benefits from the store-closing program and careful cost management.

"We are pleased that the steps we have taken to improve our business -- our store-closing and capital management programs and strategic realignment -- have reduced the first quarter pretax loss," Eugster said.

"Despite progress, it is important to note that improved borrowing flexibility and capacity from our bank group and uninterrupted shipments from our trade vendors are essential to the company's continued financial viability," he added.

First quarter revenues fell two percent to $376.1 million from $383.6 million a year ago. Sales reflected the closing of 126 stores since the first quarter of 1996, including 29 Media Play stores, offset by a comparable-store sales increase of 2.9 percent.

Looking ahead, he said Musicland faces a more difficult sales comparison in the second quarter because of the 1996 releases of audio products such as Hootie and the Blowfish and Metallica and video titles "Waiting to Exhale" and "Aristocats."
Square footage for all Musicland Stores totaled 8.4 million at March 31, down 14.6 percent from 9.9 million a year earlier.

At the end of the quarter, the company operated a total of 1,392 stores (68 Media Play stores, 156 On Cue stores, 413 Suncoast stores, 734 Sam Goody/Musicland stores, and 21 United Kingdom stores) in 49 states, the United Kingdom, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands.
